recipes.name: Robbi's M&Ms Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1.5 cups candy-coated milk chocolate pieces (such as M&M's®)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Beat shortening, brown sugar, white sugar, eggs, and vanilla in a mixing bowl until light and fluffy, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add flour, baking soda, and salt; blend well. Stir in 1/2 of the chocolate candies.
Drop dough by teaspoonfuls onto an ungreased baking sheet. Use remaining candies to decorate dough balls; press down slightly.
Bake in batches in the preheated oven until lightly browned with soft centers, 9 to 11 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Robbi's M&Ms Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This M&M cookie recipe makes soft, chewy cookies with crisp edges packed with chocolate candies that melt in your mouth. And no chill time needed!

review.reviewBody: PLEASE NOTE: At culinary school the first thing we learned about cookie making is that when you beat the butter/shortening the friction heats it up the dough. While incorporating the ingredients better it also breaks down the fat in the product. To correct this all you need to do is refrigerate you dough for about 5 minutes before baking. Doing so will re-solidify the fats and stop your cookies from over spreading. This is the base cookie recipe I use for chocolate chip and other cookies, except I use either butter or half shortnenting and half butter. It just depends on the product I am making. You will see a HUGE difference if you try this procedure, guaranteed.

Best cookies EVERR! Instead of shortening I used 2 sticks of butter and they came out PERFECT! I also didnt use so much salt and baked for a few minutes longer. Adding extra m&ms didnt hurt either! YUM!

After reading all the other reviews, I made this using a 1/2 cup of room temp butter and 1/2 cup butter flavored shortening. They spread slightly on the pan, but not a whole lot, and they had a great flavor. Also, for my oven, a bake time of 8 1/2 minutes got them pretty well baked, and then I let them sit on the pan for an additional 4 minutes, finishing it up. Perfect. I also made a batch of Chocolate Mint M & M cookies by adding a 1/2 cup cocoa to the batter and using candy covered mint pieces. Heavenly.

There is a reason this recipe has over 1000 five-star reviews. It is excellent. That said, you still have to LOOK at your dough. I have been making this recipe for years and now my daughter uses it too. I always double this recipe and I always use all butter - no shortening. I increase the flour until I get a good stiff dough (about a cup extra in a doubled recipe). This is where looking at your dough comes in. If the dough is too soft you are going to get flat nasty cookies. Your ambient humidity matters. Sometimes I do half whole wheat half all purpose flour. Lastly, I normally use parchment paper and bake at 375. This recipe is perfect every time. To the 34 people who gave it one star - try again, you did something wrong.

What a great discovery. The recipe calls for shortening, but we halved it and added butter in its place. Then we chilled the dough for 2 hours and I used a medium cookie scoop to create even balls of dough, which we flattened with the bottom of a glass, then placed m&m minis atop. It’s a BIG HIT!

I used 1/2 cup butter and 1/2 cup shortening. For the mix-ins, a cup of candies and a cup of walnuts and I used my smallest cookie scoop. Slightly larger than a teaspoon so I baked for 12 1/2 minutes. Delicious but didn’t make 72 servings.
These are delicious!! I used 1/2 cup shortening and 1/2 cup butter. I always leave any cookie batter in the fridge for 1-2 hours before baking to prevent spreading too much.

First thing I want to say is getting 6-7 dozen cookies from this recipe doesn’t seem realistic. I was able to make 4 dozen decent size cookies. Anything smaller than that, well nobody wants tiny baby cookies! I did make a few modifications. I used unsalted butter, I added half a teaspoon of vanilla, and 2/3 a cup of chocolate chips. Also, I chilled the dough for 20 minutes before baking. And in my oven 350° for 10 minutes came out perfectly. Crunchy on the outside chewy in the middle.

Made this recipe early in the morning which made my husband actually get up from the wonderful cookie aroma. He LOVED these cookies. I substituted the shortening for 2 sticks of real butter and after I had the batter completed I put it in the refrigerator for an hour before baking them . I also cooked them for the complete cooking time of 11min. I have an electric oven so this timing was perfect. They came out PERECT . Love this recipe

We ate the “best” ones right away so the picture does not do justice for how amazing these cookies are. I used half the recipe, 1 heaping teaspoon of batter on parchment paper, and got a lot of cookies. Used butter-slightly melted, sifted the dry ingredients separately and used parchment paper. SO GOOD!

I've been making this recipe for years for my boyfriend's birthday. I put vanilla ice cream between 2 cookies to make a sandwich then freeze them. Soooo much better than store bought cookie-wiches. They are also fantastic without ice cream. I make them with 1/2 cup unsalted butter and 1/2 cup shortening. I chill the dough for a bit so they don't spread too much. I LOVE these cookies and so does my boyfriend!

This recipe was so amazing, I’ve made it so many times, but I substitute the shortening for butter and the all purpose flour into wheat flour because it enhances the flavor! I’m a kid baker, but I bake by myself.
I used butter instead of shortening. Personal preference.
Used butter flavored crisco and gluten free flour, perfect

I think there's too much butter in this recipe. When I baked the cookies right after mixing, they all spread into eachother and made one giant, underbaked sheet pan cookie. Then I chilled the dough for an hour and tried baking again. They didnt spread as much, but they did get way too brown around the edges before the centers were even done. Pretty disappointed.

This is the recipe that my mom used to make, and I’m happy that you posted it. I hadn’t bout Crisco for years but I remember that is what she used to use in cookie recipes. So I bought some Crisco and used half Crisco, and half butter in this recipe. Like others have mentioned, I recommend chilling the dough before baking.

My family absolutely loved these. Based on other reviews I made just a couple small tweaks. I used 2 sticks of butter (1 salted and 1 unsalted because that's what I had) instead of the shortening. I also used slightly less salt than was called for. I rolled them into 1 ounce balls of dough and this made 38 cookies.
Great cookie recipe- and yes, 1/2 cup butter and 1/2 cup shortening.

I like the recipe. The recipe is fine. However the dough was incredibly wet. It was insanely like sticky. I added more than 2 1/2 cups of flour because the dough was so wet and the cookies spread and had yucky flats. More flour firmed up the dough just right and helped them hold their shape. Anyone who’s ever baked cookies would know that the dough was just too wet. And that’s why people had problems with flat cookies is because there’s just not enough flour. The taste is okay. It reminds me of store bought cookies and the flavor is just okay I feel like. Definitely would recommend more mms though. I ran out and had to buy more. Each cookies has a small amount for the size of the batch. Definitely could use more candies. I wouldn’t say this is a huge banger like most of the 5 star say. Definitely needs work on this recipe
Subbed butter for hydrogenated vegetable oil. Made with valentine m&m's. Would chill dough or dough balls before baking next time.
